conclusion: Reading the joined OGRE 14 scene costs 20.82 ms, 68.6 percent of a 30.33 ms frame. Snapshot production, which a native scene source would still perform, costs 0.358 ms.
notes: The OGRE 14 scene path - producing the scene in OGRE 14 and then reading it back out - accounts for 25.33 ms of the 30.33 ms frame.

Snapshot production and normalization are together under 1.5 percent, so the renderer-neutral conversion itself is not the cost. Neither is the GPU: dispatch, render submission and completion wait total 4.10 ms.

This supersedes the producer attribution recorded in OGRE_NEXT_PHASE_ATTRIBUTION_M5_2026-08-17.json, which attributed only UpdateScene to the producer and concluded that removing it would save about 4.5 ms. The scene read belongs to the same coupling; removing the OGRE 14 scene path addresses both.

Removing that path leaves dispatch, production and remainder, about 5 ms. That is a projection from measured stage costs, not a measured result: a native scene source will have its own cost, which is not yet known.
scene_dispatch's 63.34 ms maximum against a 4.10 ms mean shows occasional presentation stalls that the mean does not describe.
